ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a net of a cube. The middle row, from left to right, is the numbers 6, 2, 4, 5, where 2 is in the second square of this row. The square with the number 1 is above 2, and the square with the number 3 is below 2. Reasoning: When the net is folded into a cube, taking the face with the number 2 as a reference, 1 and 3 are folded to the opposite upper and lower faces respectively, so 1 and 3 are opposite; 6 and 4 are folded to the opposite left and right faces respectively, so 6 and 4 are opposite; the rightmost 5 will be folded to the position opposite 2, so 2 and 5 are opposite. The three faces that meet at one vertex of a cube cannot contain a pair of opposite faces, so each vertex takes exactly one face from each of the three groups of opposite faces (1,3), (6,4), (2,5). To make the sum the largest, take the larger number in each group respectively: max(1,3)=3, max(6,4)=6, max(2,5)=5. The maximum sum is 3+6+5=14. Final answer: 14

method.method_draft: Read the net as four squares in a horizontal row labeled 6, 2, 4, 5, with square 1 above 2 and square 3 below 2. Use the face labeled 2 as a reference when folding: 1 and 3 fold to opposite top/bottom faces, 6 and 4 fold to opposite left/right faces, and the far square 5 folds around to become opposite face 2. Thus the opposite pairs are (1,3), (6,4), and (2,5). Since three faces meeting at any cube corner must contain exactly one face from each opposite pair, the largest possible corner sum is obtained by choosing the larger number from each pair: max(1,3)+max(6,4)+max(2,5)=3+6+5=14.
